title: Using declarations and using directives
recap: A qualified name identifies its scope explicitly, such as Shipping::status. A using-declaration makes one selected qualified name available unqualified within its scope, whereas a using-directive makes every name in a namespace eligible for unqualified lookup.

Explicit qualification is clearest and avoids accidental collisions. A focused using-declaration can be acceptable in a source-file block after includes, but using-directives and using-statements in headers expose code to current and future naming conflicts.
objectives: Use one block-scoped using-declaration for a selected namespace member.
Keep a same-named member from another namespace explicitly qualified.
Distinguish qualified and unqualified name use.
warnings: Do not use using namespace std or another using-directive to save typing.
Do not put using-statements in headers or before include directives.
An unqualified name can become ambiguous when multiple visible namespaces offer the same identifier.
challenge: Define Inventory::status and Shipping::status as distinct constexpr string views. Inside main, use a block-scoped using-declaration that introduces only Inventory::status, print that name unqualified, and print Shipping::status with explicit qualification.
hints: Both namespace members may have the same identifier because their qualified names differ.
Place using Inventory::status inside main after the opening brace.
Do not introduce Shipping::status; qualify that use directly.
